requirements.text: The ESA sample(s) shall be clearly and indelibly marked with the manufacturer's trade name or mark and the type designation.
An approval mark as described in paragraph 5.3 shall be affixed to every ESA conforming to a type approved under UN R10.
The ESA shall be designed, constructed and fitted in such a way as to enable the vehicle, in normal conditions of use, to comply with the requirements of UN R10.
The ESA shall comply with the requirements for radiated and conducted emissions.
The ESA shall comply with the requirements for immunity to radiated and conducted disturbances.
The electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall comply with the limits when measured by the method described in Annex 7.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed 62 to 52 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed 52 to 63 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz, as shown in Appendix 6.

Where measured using the method described in Annex 7, the broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed a constant limit of 63 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband values, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 8.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 52 to 42 dB microvolts/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall be 42 to 53 dB microvolts/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 7.
If measurements are made using the method described in Annex 8, the ESA narrowband type approval limit shall remain constant at 53 dB microvolts/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured narrowband value, expressed in dB microvolts/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2 as described in Annex 10 for the levels given in Table 1.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA shall be +75 V.
For vehicles with 12 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA shall be -100 V.
For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA shall be +150 V.
For vehicles with 24 V systems, the maximum allowed negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA shall be -450 V.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) chosen from those described in Annex 9.
The immunity to electromagnetic radiation of the ESA representative of its type shall be tested by the method(s) as described in Annex 9.

Where the stripline method is used, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2a.
Where the TEM cell method is used, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 75 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2a.
Where the BCI method is used, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 60 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2a.

Where the ALSE method is used, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 30 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 10 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2a.

Where the reverberation chamber method is used, the ESA shall withstand a test level of 21 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 7 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range in over 90 per cent of the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2a.
Where the stripline method is used, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 V/m in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2b.
Where the TEM cell method is used, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 62,5 V/m in the 20 to 200 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2b.
Where the BCI method is used, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 50 mA in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2b.

Where the ALSE method is used, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 25 V/m in the 80 to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 8 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2b.

Where the reverberation chamber method is used, the ESA shall withstand a minimum test level of 18 V/m in the LUF to 2,000 MHz frequency range and 6 V/m in the 2,000 to 6,000 MHz frequency range over the whole 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency band, as given in Table 2b.
The ESA representative of its type shall show no degradation of performance of "immunity related functions" during the tests performed in accordance with Annex 9.

The immunity of the ESA representative of its type to transient disturbances conducted along 12/24 V supply lines shall be tested according to ISO 16750-2 for the starting profile and ISO 7637-2 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b, as described in Annex 10, with the test levels given in Tables 3a and 3b.

The ESA shall meet the starting profile test according to the functional status classification as defined in ISO 16750-1, only where the ESA could be installed in vehicles with internal combustion engines which are started with a 12V/24V starter motor.

For the starting profile, the ESA shall withstand immunity test level II for 12 V systems and level II for 24 V systems with 10 pulses, achieving functional status B for immunity related functions where the ESA shall be operational during engine start phases, C for other ESA, and D for functions not related to immunity related functions.
The ESA shall meet the Functional Performance Status Classification (FPSC) as in ISO 7637-1 for pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b.

For test pulse 1, the ESA shall withstand -75 V for 12 V systems and -450 V for 24 V systems for 500 pulses with FPSC III for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2a, the ESA shall withstand +37 V for 12 V systems and +37 V for 24 V systems for 500 pulses with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 2b, the ESA shall withstand +10 V for 12 V systems and +20 V for 24 V systems for 10 pulses with FPSC II for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3a, the ESA shall withstand -112 V for 12 V systems and -150 V for 24 V systems for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.

For test pulse 3b, the ESA shall withstand +75 V for 12 V systems and +150 V for 24 V systems for 1 h with FPSC I for immunity related functions and III for functions not related to immunity related functions.
Where the ESA does not include an electronic oscillator with an operating frequency greater than 9 kHz, it shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.3.2. or 6.6.2. and with Annexes 5 and 8.
Where the ESA has no immunity related functions, it need not be tested for immunity to radiated disturbances and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.8. and with Annex 9.

Where the ESA is not switched, contains no switches or does not include inductive load, it need not be tested for emission of transient conducted disturbances on 12/24 V supply lines and shall be deemed to comply with paragraph 6.7.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation generated by the ESA representative of its type shall be measured by the method described in Annex 7.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission type approval limit shall be 62 to 52 dBµV/m in the 30 to 75 MHz frequency band, this limit decreasing logarithmically with frequencies above 30 MHz.

Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission type approval limit shall be 52 to 63 dBµV/m in the 75 to 400 MHz band, this limit increasing logarithmically with frequencies above 75 MHz as shown in Appendix 6.
Where measurements are made using the method described in Annex 7, the ESA broadband radiated emission type approval limit shall remain constant at 63 dBµV/m in the 400 to 1,000 MHz frequency band.
On the ESA representative of its type, the measured broadband emission values, expressed in dBµV/m, shall be below the type approval limits.

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA representative of its type on 12 / 24 V supply lines shall be tested by the method(s) according to ISO 7637-2:2011, as described in Annex 10, for the levels given in Table 18.
The positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA on supply lines shall not exceed +75 V for vehicles with 12 V systems.
The positive pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA on supply lines shall not exceed +150 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
The negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA on supply lines shall not exceed -100 V for vehicles with 12 V systems.
The negative pulse amplitude of transient conducted emissions generated by the ESA on supply lines shall not exceed -450 V for vehicles with 24 V systems.
ESAs approved under UN R10 shall be so manufactured as to conform to the type approved by meeting the requirements set forth in paragraph 6 and, if applicable, in paragraph 7 of UN R10.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed the limit E = 62 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F in the range 30-75 MHz for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed the limit E = 52 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F in the range 75-400 MHz for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The broadband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed the limit E = 63 dBµV/m in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed the limit E = 52 - 25.13 log (F/30) dBµV/m at frequency F in the range 30-75 MHz for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed the limit E = 42 + 15.13 log (F/75) dBµV/m at frequency F in the range 75-400 MHz for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The narrowband electromagnetic radiation of the ESA shall not exceed the limit E = 53 dBµV/m in the frequency range 400-1,000 MHz for a 120 kHz bandwidth.
The approval mark with regard to electromagnetic compatibility affixed to a vehicle or ESA shall have the dimension a of 6 mm min, as shown in the examples of approval marks in Annex 1.
The broadband electromagnetic emissions from the ESA shall be tested according to CISPR 25, if not otherwise stated in Annex 7.
For an ESA other than one involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid", the broadband emission test shall be performed according to the ALSE method described in Clause 6.4 of CISPR 25.

The ESA shall comply with the broadband emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The ESA shall meet the narrowband electromagnetic emission limits throughout the frequency range 30 to 1,000 MHz for measurements performed in an absorber lined shielded enclosure (ALSE) or open area test site (OATS).

The ESA other than an ESA involved in "REESS charging mode coupled to the power grid" shall comply with the immunity requirements of any combination, at the manufacturer's discretion, of the absorber chamber test according to ISO 11452-2, TEM cell testing according to ISO 11452-3, bulk current injection testing according to ISO 11452-4, stripline testing according to ISO 11452-5 and reverberation chamber test according to ISO 11452-11, provided that these results cover the full frequency range specified in paragraph 3.1. of Annex 9, with frequency range and general test conditions based on ISO 11452-1.
The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements of Annex 9 in the 20 to 6,000 MHz frequency range, with frequency steps, frequency step size and dwell time according to ISO 11452-1.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements of Annex 9 with AM (amplitude modulation) test signal modulation, with 1 kHz modulation and 80 per cent modulation depth, in the 20 to 400 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements of Annex 9 with PM2 (pulse modulation type 2) test signal modulation, Ton 3 µs, period 3,333 µs, in the 2,700 to 3,100 MHz frequency range, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall meet the immunity requirements of Annex 9 with PM3 (pulse modulation type 3) test signal modulation, Ton 500 µs, period 1,000 µs, in the 380 to 2,700 MHz and the 3,100 to 6,000 MHz frequency ranges, if not otherwise agreed between Technical Service and ESA manufacturer.

The ESA shall withstand test pulses 1, 2a, 2b, 3a and 3b according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2 applied to its 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines.

The ESA shall withstand the starting profile according to the International Standard ISO 16750-2 applied to its 12/24 V supply lines as well as to other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, except for ESAs that are exclusively reserved for mounting on electric vehicles (vehicles without 12V/24V starter motor).

The emission of transient conducted disturbances generated by the ESA on 12/24 V supply lines, as well as on other connections of the ESA which may be operationally connected to supply lines, shall be measured according to the International Standard ISO 7637-2.
Each lamp that is part of the same unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps shall satisfy the provisions set out in UN Regulation No. 148 or in another Regulation.
Lamps not satisfying the provisions of any of those Regulations shall not be part of a unit of grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps.
Every device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraphs 3.3.3.2. to 3.3.3.6.
All markings on the device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The value for "a" of the approval marking shall be at least 5 mm.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number, being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The four to six-digit sequential number of the approval number shall be placed close to the approval mark.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of front or rear position lamps and front or rear end-outline marker lamps.

On lamps which cannot be mounted on either side of the vehicle indiscriminately, the horizontal arrow showing the mounting position shall be directed outwards from the vehicle in the case of reversing lamps in case of reduced light distribution of two reversing lamps.
Lamps shall bear the approval marking.
Lamps shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.
Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall bear a marking indicating the category or categories of light source(s) prescribed.

Lamps, with the exception of lamps with non-replaceable light sources, shall, in the case where the lamp has been approved for LED substitute light source(s), also bear a marking indicating the category or categories of the LED substitute light source(s).
Lamps with an electronic light source control gear shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with a variable luminous intensity control shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with a secondary operating mode shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
Lamps with non-replaceable light sources shall bear marking of the rated voltage(s) (i.e. 6V, 12V or 24V) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the specific identification code of the module, comprising the starting letters "MD" for "MODULE" followed by the approval mark without the circle.
In case several non-identical replaceable light source modules are used, the specific identification code of each module shall be followed by additional symbols or characters.
The approval mark on the replaceable light source module and the approval mark on the lamp in which the module is used shall be from the same applicant, although they do not have to be the same.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the light source module(s) shall bear the rated voltage(s) or the range of voltage.
In case replaceable light source module(s) is/are used, the lamp shall bear the specific identification code of the module as prescribed in paragraph 3.3.3.5. (a), (ii).

An electronic light source control gear or variable luminous intensity control being part of the lamp, but not included into the lamp body, shall be marked with its identification number and the name of the manufacturer.
The approval marking shall be placed on an inner or outer part (transparent or not) of the lamp which is not designed to be separated from the transparent part of the lamp emitting the light.

The approval marking, as well as the category or categories of LED substitute light source(s) prescribed, if any, shall be visible when the lamp is fitted on the vehicle or when a movable part such as the hood or boot lid or a door is opened.
If the outer lens of a device is designed to be separated from the main body, the approval marking shall be placed on both the detachable lens and the main body.
In case an outer lens is used for several devices and bears different approval markings, the main body of each device shall bear only the approval marking of the function(s) of that device.
The approval marking and the markings in paragraphs 3.3.3.2., 3.3.3.3., 3.3.3.4., 3.3.3.5. (b) and 3.3.3.6. shall be affixed on the lamp.
The markings in paragraph 3.3.3.5.(a) shall be affixed on the component.

Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.
Each lamp submitted for approval shall conform to the requirements set forth in paragraphs 4. and 5. of UN R148.

The lamp shall comply with the requirements contained in sections 5 "General specifications" and 6 "Individual specifications" (and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections) of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the lamp type approval, as pertinent to each lamp and to the category/ies of vehicle on which the lamp is intended to be installed, where its verification at the moment of lamp type approval is feasible.

The lamps shall be so designed and constructed that in normal conditions of use, and notwithstanding the vibrations to which they may be subjected in such use, their satisfactory operation remains assured and they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN R148.

In the case of a rear position lamp reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp, using a common light source and designed to operate permanently with an additional system to regulate the intensity of the light emitted, these functions shall either be provided by multiple light sources (for instance, a double filament light source) or be intended for use in a vehicle equipped with a tell-tale indicating failure for the lamps.

Where the internal structure of the optical components and/or the texture of the outer lens inside the apparent surface of a lamp (function) incorporates a manufacturer logo, it shall incorporate only one manufacturer logo built by transparent or non-transparent components and all requirements for the specific function of UN R148 shall be fulfilled.

Where a logo is incorporated inside the apparent surface of a lamp, only the logo of the brand name of the vehicle manufacturer or the body manufacturer shall be allowed, irrespective of the marking requirements in paragraph 3.3.

Where a logo is incorporated inside the apparent surface of a lamp, the enclosed light emitting surface of the logo (incorporating transparent and non-transparent components of the logo) in the direction of the reference axis shall not exceed 100 cm2.
Stop lamps, direction indicator lamps, and reversing lamps shall not incorporate a logo.

In a single lamp containing more than one light source, a group of light sources wired so that the failure of any one of them causes all of them to stop emitting light shall be considered to be one light source.

In case of failure of any one light source in a single lamp containing more than one light source, either the light intensity shall comply with the minimum intensity required in the pertinent table of standard light distribution as shown in Annex 3, with the maximum intensities not exceeded when all light sources are illuminated, or a signal for activation of a tell-tale indicating failure, as indicated in paragraphs 6.4.8., 6.7.8., 6.9.8, 6.10.8., 6.11.8., 6.12.8., 6.13.8. and 6.18.8. of UN Regulation No. 48, shall be produced, in which case the lamp is only for use on a vehicle fitted with a tell-tale indicating failure.

The lamp shall only be equipped with replaceable light source(s) approved according to UN Regulations Nos. 37, 99 and/or 128, provided that no restriction on the use is made at the time of application for type approval, and/or light source module(s) and/or non-replaceable light source(s).
Light Signalling Devices shall not generate radiated or power line disturbances which cause a malfunction of other electric/electronic systems of the vehicle.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it can only be fitted in the designated and correct position and can only be removed with the use of tool(s).
In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that it is tamperproof.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, regardless of the use of tool(s), it is not interchangeable with any replaceable UN approved light source and/or any other replaceable light source module having different characteristics that is located in the same lamp housing.

In case of replaceable light source module(s), the design of the light source module(s) shall be such that, when the light source module is removed and replaced by another module provided by the applicant and bearing the same light source module identification code, the photometric requirements of the device are met.
In the case of a lamp equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the photometric and colorimetric requirements shall be met with the light source(s) present in the lamp.

Where the lamp may be installed on the vehicle in more than one or in a field of different positions, the photometric requirements shall be met for each position or for the extreme positions of the field of the reference axis specified by the manufacturer.
If not otherwise specified, the luminous intensities of the light-signalling lamp shall be measured with the light source continuously lit.
Unless otherwise specified, the voltage supplied at the lamp for testing shall be either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).
In case of a lamp controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control, the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant.

In the case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and equipped with light source module(s) or non-replaceable light source(s), the lamp shall be operated for testing as specified by the applicant, with the voltage supplied at the lamp, unless otherwise specified, being either 6.75 V (6 Volt-Systems), 13.5 V (12 Volt-Systems) or 28 V (24 Volt-Systems).

In the case of a lamp not controlled by an electronic light source control gear or a variable intensity control and equipped with replaceable UN approved light source(s), the light sources shall be operated for testing at the reference/objective luminous flux or alternatively at a different luminous flux with a proportional correction on the measured luminous intensities.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, on the reference axis (HV), be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, in no direction where the lamp is visible, exceed the maximum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, outside the reference axis, be not less than the product of the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5. by the percentage specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question, or be not less than the intensity value as specified in the pertinent light distribution figure reproduced in Annex 3 for each direction in question.

If not otherwise specified, the intensity of light emitted by each of the two samples supplied shall, within the angles of geometric visibility defined in the tables in Annex 2, be not less than the minimum specified in the table of the pertinent function in paragraph 5.
The luminous intensity of the lamp shall observe the provisions of the relevant paragraphs of Annex 3 on local variations of intensity.

Where the applicant requests the additional test to verify the visibility of red light towards the front and/or white light towards the rear of a vehicle required in UN Regulation No. 48, the maximum intensity of the lamp in the angular field from 165° to 180° outboard in horizontal direction and -2.5° to +5° in vertical direction shall be not more than 2.5∙10-1 cd, which may be verified taking into account the influence of the vehicle body.

When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for maximum intensity if all lamps together are lit.

When an assembly of two independent lamps, to be type approved as lamps marked "D" and having the same function, is deemed to be a single lamp, it shall comply with the requirements for minimum intensity if either lamp has failed.
An interdependent lamp system shall meet the luminous intensity requirements when all its interdependent lamps are operated together.

If the interdependent lamp system providing the rear position lamp is partly mounted on the fixed component and partly mounted on a movable component, the interdependent lamp(s) specified by the applicant shall meet the outboard geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirement at all fixed positions of the movable component(s), the inboard geometric visibility requirement being deemed satisfied if this (these) interdependent lamp(s) still conform to the photometric values prescribed in the field of light distribution for the approval of the device at all fixed positions of the moveable component(s).

If a rear position lamp and/or a rear end-outline marker lamp is reciprocally incorporated with a stop lamp producing either steady or variable luminous intensity, the ratio between the luminous intensities actually measured of the two lamps when turned on simultaneously and the intensity of the rear position lamp or end-outline marker lamp when turned on alone should be at least 5:1 in the field delimited by the straight horizontal lines passing through ±5° V and the straight vertical lines passing through ±10° H of the light distribution table, with the values obtained with all sources in operation being considered where one or both of the two reciprocally incorporated lamps contain(s) more than one light source and is (are) considered as a single lamp.
The luminous intensities of the lamp shall comply with the requirements when tested according to Annex 8.

The colour of the light emitted shall comply with the colorimetric requirements when measured inside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in the relevant paragraph of Annex 3, using the test procedure described in paragraph 4.8.
Outside the field of the light distribution grid defined for the specific function in Annex 3, no sharp variation of colour of the light emitted shall be observed.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the colorimetric characteristics should be verified with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 4.8.

For lamps (functions) using different light source technologies, the colorimetric characteristics shall be met for each light source technology separately according to the applicable provisions in paragraphs 4.8.1. and 4.8.2.

The light emitted by each of the two samples of the rear position lamp or rear end-outline marker lamp supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 4.

For rear position lamps reciprocally incorporated with stop lamps, a luminous intensity of 6.0∙10^1 cd shall be permitted below a plane forming an angle of 5° with and downward from the horizontal plane.
For rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps of categories R1, MR or RM1 (steady), the minimum luminous intensity shall be 4∙10^0 cd.
For rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps of categories R1, MR or RM1 (steady), the maximum luminous intensity shall be 1.7∙10^1 cd when used as a single lamp.
For rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps of categories R1, MR or RM1 (steady), the maximum luminous intensity shall be 8.5∙10^0 cd for a lamp marked "D" (paragraph 3.3.2.5.2.).
For rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps of categories R1, MR or RM1 (steady), the standard light distribution shall be as defined in Figure A3-I.

For rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps of categories R1, MR or RM1 (steady), the angles of geometric visibility shall be as defined in Table A2-1 with a minimum luminous intensity of 5∙10^-2 cd.
The minimum luminous intensity of rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps within the angles of geometric visibility shall be as specified in Table 4 (5∙10^-2 cd).
Rear position lamps and rear end-outline marker lamps shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the rear position lamp (R1, R2, MR) and the rear end-outline marker lamp (RM1, RM2) shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of stop lamp (S1, S2, S3, S4, MS) supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 7.
The minimum luminous intensity of an S1 (steady) stop lamp shall be 6.0∙10^1 cd.
The maximum luminous intensity of an S1 (steady) stop lamp shall be 2.60∙10^2 cd when used as a single lamp and 1.30∙10^2 cd for a lamp marked "D".
The standard light distribution of an S1 (steady) stop lamp shall be as defined in Figure A3-I.
The minimum luminous intensity of an S1 (steady) stop lamp within the angles of geometric visibility defined in Table A2-1 shall be 3∙10^-1 cd.
The stop lamp (S1, S2, S3, S4, MS) shall meet the minimum luminous intensity within the angles of geometric visibility specified in Table 7.
The stop lamp (S1, S2, S3, S4, MS) shall meet the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by the stop lamp (S1, S2, S3, S4, MS) shall be red.
The light emitted by each of the two samples of reversing lamp (AR) supplied shall meet the luminous intensity and standard light distribution requirements in Table 10.

Where the reversing lamp is intended to be installed on a vehicle exclusively in a pair of devices and its photometric intensity is verified only up to an angle of 30° inwards, a photometric value of at least 2.5∙10^1 cd shall be satisfied at that angle.
Where the reversing lamp is type approved under the condition of verification only up to 30° inwards, the device shall only be installed in a pair.
The minimum luminous intensity of a reversing lamp of category AR shall be 8.0∙10^1 cd.
The maximum luminous intensity of a reversing lamp of category AR above the h-plane shall be 3.00∙10^2 cd.
The maximum luminous intensity of a reversing lamp of category AR in or below the h-plane down to 5°D shall be 6.00∙10^2 cd.
The maximum luminous intensity of a reversing lamp of category AR below 5°D shall be 8.00∙10^3 cd.
The standard light distribution of a reversing lamp of category AR shall be as specified in Figure A3-V.
Reversing lamps (AR) shall comply with the failure provisions of paragraph 4.6.
The colour of light emitted by reversing lamps (AR) shall be white.

The front/rear position lamp (A, R1, R2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 80° outboard, or 20°/80° (reduced angles used only below the H-plane) for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.

The front/rear position lamp (A, R1, R2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below, or 15°/5° for lamps to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, or 5°/15° for optional lamps to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm.

The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum horizontal angles of geometric visibility of 45° inboard / 45° outboard, or 20°/45° (reduced angles used only below the H-plane) for lamps mounted with the H-plane below 750 mm.

The stop lamp (S1, S2) shall have minimum vertical angles of geometric visibility of 15° above / 15° below, or 15°/5° for lamps to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of less than 750 mm, or 5°/15° for optional lamps to be installed with the H-plane of the lamp at a mounting height of more than 2,100 mm.

Unless specified otherwise, the lamp shall meet, for the various directions of measurement relative to the reference axis (H = 0°, V = 0°) passing through the centre of reference, the minimum intensities given in Figures A3-I to A3-XV as a percentage of the minimum intensities required, mathematically rounded down to three significant digits.

Where front and rear position lamps are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Where stop lamps of category S1, S2 and MS are intended to be installed at a mounting height (using the H plane specified by the manufacturer) equal to or less than 750 mm above the ground, the photometric intensity shall be verified only up to an angle of 5° downwards.

Within the field of light distribution shown as a grid, the light intensity of the lamp in each direction of a part of the field formed by the grid lines shall meet at least the lowest minimum value shown as a percentage on the grid lines surrounding the questioned direction.

For reversing lamps, if visual examination appears to reveal substantial local variations of intensity, no intensity measured between two of the directions of measurement shall be below 50 per cent of the lower minimum intensity of the two prescribed for these directions of measurement.

Front and rear position lamps and stop lamps (S1, S2 and MS) shall meet, for the various directions of measurement, the minimum intensities given by the standard light distribution as a percentage of the minimum intensities required (see Tables 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8).

The reversing lamp shall meet the minimum intensities of the light emitted at the measuring points, expressed in degrees of angle with the axis of reference, given by the standard light distribution for reversing lamps.

The reversing lamp shall meet, for the various directions of measurement relative to the axis of reference (H = 0°, V = 0°) passing through the centre of reference, the minimum intensities in cd shown in Figure A3-V.
The photometric performances of any mass-produced lamp chosen at random shall comply with the requirements when tested according to paragraph 4.8. of this Regulation.
The lamp shall comply with the chromaticity coordinates when tested under the conditions of paragraph 4.9. of this Regulation.

The lamp shall withstand a one-hour test of continuous operation following a warm-up period of 20 minutes at an ambient temperature of 23 °C ± 5 °C, with a light source of the category specified for the lamp supplied with a current at a voltage such that it gives the specified average power at the corresponding test voltage.

For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources (filament light sources and other), the heat resistance test shall be made with the light sources present in the lamp, in accordance with paragraph 5.4.5. of this Regulation.

Where only the maximum power is specified, the lamp shall withstand the heat resistance test with the voltage regulated to obtain a power equal to 90 per cent of the specified power, chosen from the rated voltage(s) of 6, 12 or 24 V at which it reaches the highest value.
For lamps equipped with non-replaceable light sources, the heat resistance test conditions set in paragraph 5.4.5. or 5.9.5. of this Regulation shall be applied.
After the heat resistance test and after the lamp has been stabilized at the ambient temperature, no distortion, deformation, cracking or colour modification of the lamp shall be perceptible.

In case of doubt, the intensity of light of the lamp measured according to paragraph 5. of this Regulation after the heat resistance test shall reach at least 90 per cent of the values obtained before the heat resistance test on the same lamp.

For reversing lamps and manoeuvring lamps using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, the luminous intensities measured after 1 minute and after 10 minutes of operation shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

For lamps (functions) using light source technologies other than incandescent technology, other than those covered by paragraph 1.2.1, the luminous intensities measured after 1 min and either after 30 minutes of operation or after photometric stability has occurred shall comply with the minimum and maximum requirements.

In case a lamp (function) uses any other light generating technology, the corresponding intensity requirements of the lamp (function) shall be complied with at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and up to when photometric stability is reached.

In case of doubt (e.g. unexpected run-up behaviour), the lamp (function) shall comply with the corresponding minimum intensity requirements at all points in time starting at the corresponding point in time listed in Table A8-1 and ending when photometric stability is reached.
The approval number assigned to each approved type of retro-reflective device shall be marked on the device following the requirements of paragraph 3.3.
The retro-reflector for motor vehicles (independent) shall be identified by the symbol IA, with a minimum approval-marking dimension "a" of 5 mm, and shall meet the requirements of paragraph 5.1.

The retro-reflector for motor vehicles combined with other signal lamps which are not watertight shall be identified by the symbol IB, with a minimum approval-marking dimension "a" of 5 mm, and shall meet the requirements of paragraph 5.1.

Every retro-reflective device belonging to an approved type shall comprise a space of sufficient size for the Unique Identifier as referred to in the 1958 Agreement and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2., or for the approval marking and other markings as defined in paragraph 3.3.4.2.
All markings on the retro-reflective device shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval marking shall include the four to six-digit sequential number being part of the approval number prescribed in paragraph 3.2.3.2.
The sequential number shall be placed close to the approval mark.
Where the approval marking as defined in paragraph 3.3.2. is replaced by the Unique Identifier, the Unique Identifier mark shall follow the format in the example shown in the regulation.
Retro-reflective devices shall bear the trade name or mark of the applicant.

In case of a retro-reflector of Class IA, IIIA, IB, IIIB or IVA, the retro-reflective device shall bear the word "TOP" inscribed horizontally on the highest part of the illuminating surface, if such an indication is necessary to determine without ambiguity the angle or angles of rotation prescribed by the manufacturer.

The approval marking or the Unique Identifier and the markings required for retro-reflective devices (trade name or mark and, where applicable, "TOP") shall be clearly legible on the retro-reflective device.

Where a single approval mark is affixed to grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated lamps, the size of the components of the single approval mark shall not be less than the minimum size required for the smallest of the individual marks by the pertinent UN Regulations under which approval has been granted.

The retro-reflecting device shall meet the requirements contained in sections 5. "General specifications" and 6. "Individual specifications" and in the Annexes referenced in the said sections of UN Regulations Nos. 48, 53, 74 or 86, and their series of amendments in force at the time of application for the retro-reflecting device type approval, pertinent to the retro-reflecting device and to the category/ies of vehicle on which it is intended to be installed, where its verification at the moment of retro-reflecting device type approval is feasible.
Retro-reflective devices shall be so constructed that they function satisfactorily and will continue to do so in normal use.
Retro-reflective devices shall not have any defect in design or manufacture that is detrimental to their efficient operation or to their maintenance in good condition.
The components of retro-reflective devices or parts thereof shall not be capable of being easily dismantled.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall be easy to clean.
The outer surface of retro-reflective devices shall not be rough and any protuberances they may exhibit shall not prevent easy cleaning.
There shall be no access to the inner surface of the retro-reflectors when in normal use.
Where a retro-reflector consists of a combined retro-reflecting optical unit and filter, the optical unit and filter shall be so designed that they cannot be separated under normal conditions of use.
The retro-reflecting optical units and filters shall not be coloured by means of paint or varnish.

The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous intensity of the retro-reflective device, when illuminated by CIE Standard Illuminant A with an angle of divergence of 1/3° and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° (or, if this produces a colourless surface reflection, an angle as specified in Annex 4, Part 1, paragraph 1.1.), shall be within the limits for the night-time colour of the light retro-reflected from that device, as defined in UN Regulation No. 48.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the dimensions and shape requirements set forth in Annex 5.
Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the photometric and colorimetric requirements as specified in paragraphs 5.1.4. to 5.1.5.

Every retro-reflector of the Classes IA and IB, when tested according to paragraph 5.1.7., shall meet the physical and mechanical requirements set forth in paragraph 5.1.7., depending on the nature of the materials and construction of the retro-reflective devices.

The Class IA and IB retro-reflector shall withstand the heat resistance test described in Part 1 of Annex 6 and at least one hour after this test meet the colorimetric characteristics of paragraph 5.1.5. and the RI of paragraph 5.1.4. for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in the position defined in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.
The Class IA and IB retro-reflector shall withstand the water penetration test (Part 2 of Annex 6) followed by the tests for resistance to fuels and lubricants (Parts 1 and 2 of Annex 7).

The Class IA and IB retro-reflector shall, if necessary, withstand the corrosion test in Part 4 of Annex 6 followed by the abrasive-strength test of the rear face of the retro-reflective device in Part 5 of Annex 6.
The Class IA and IB retro-reflector shall meet the test for stability in time of the optical properties of retro-reflective device in Part 3 of Annex 4.
The Class IA and IB retro-reflector shall withstand the resistance to weathering test (Part 6 of Annex 6).

After undergoing the tests referred to in paragraph 5.1.3.1., the retro-reflectors in each group shall have an RI which satisfies the conditions laid down in paragraph 5.1.4., verified only for an angle of divergence of 20' and an illumination angle of β1 = β2 = 0° or, if necessary, in all positions specified in Part 1 of Annex 4, paragraphs 1.1. and 1.2.

Where more than one or a range of different axes of reference are specified by the manufacturer, the retro-reflector shall meet the photometric requirements with reference each time to a different axis of reference or to the extreme axis of reference of the range specified by the manufacturer.

For photometric measurements of a Class IA or IB retro-reflector, only the illuminating surface defined by the planes contiguous to the outermost parts of the optical system of the retro-reflective device as indicated by the manufacturer and contained within a circle of 200 mm diameter shall be considered, and the illuminating surface itself shall be limited to 100 cm2, though the surfaces of the retro-reflecting optical units need not necessarily attain this area.

When measured as described in paragraph 3 of Part 1 of Annex 4, the RI values for red retro-reflectors of Class IA and Class IB shall be equal to or greater than those in Table 3, expressed in millicandelas per lux, for the angles of divergence and illumination shown.
The RI value of a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 20' shall be at least 3.00∙10² mcd·lx-1 at illumination angles β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°.
The RI value of a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 20' shall be at least 1.00∙10² mcd·lx-1 at illumination angles β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°.
The RI value of a red Class IA or IB retro-reflector at an angle of divergence of 1°30' shall be at least 5∙10⁰ mcd·lx-1 at illumination angles β1 = 0°, β2 = 0°.

The retro-reflector shall not have RI values lower than those shown in the last two columns of Table 3 within the solid angle having the centre of reference as its apex and bounded by the planes intersecting along the lines (β1 = ±10°, β2 = 0°) and (β1 = ±5°, β2 = ±20°).

Where a retro-reflector of Class IA or Class IB is intended to be installed with its H plane at a mounting height less than 750 mm above the ground, the RI values of the retro-reflector shall be required to be met only up to an angle of 5° downwards.
The trichromatic coordinates of the reflected luminous flux of the retro-reflector shall be within the limits for the night-time colours red, amber or white as specified in UN Regulation No. 48.

Retro-reflective devices which are not marked "TOP", when rotated about their axes of reference to the position of minimum RI with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20', shall have a minimum RI that conforms to the value specified in paragraph 5. of this Regulation.

The RI of retro-reflective devices marked "TOP" shall not fall below the prescribed value in any position assumed by the device during rotation about their axes of ±5° with an illumination angle β of β1 = β2 = 0°, or the angle specified in paragraph 4. of this Regulation, and an angle of divergence of 20'.

The shape of the illuminating surfaces shall not be easily confused with the triangular shape, as prescribed for retro-reflectors mentioned in paragraph 2.1., from an observation distance of 10 metres.

Moulded plastics reflectors of retro-reflecting devices of Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA, SMV and advance warning triangle of type 1 shall withstand being kept for 48 consecutive hours in a dry atmosphere at a temperature of 65 °C ± 2 °C followed by cooling for 1 hour at 23 °C ± 2 °C.
After the heat resistance test, no cracking or appreciable distortion of the retro-reflective device and, in particular, of its optical component shall be visible.

Retro-reflective devices, whether part of a lamp or not, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand immersion for 10 minutes in water at a temperature of 50 °C ± 5 °C with the highest point of the upper part of the illuminating surface 20 mm below the surface of the water, repeated after turning the device through 180° so that the illuminating surface is at the bottom and the rear face is covered by about 20 mm of water, followed immediately by immersion in the same conditions in water at a temperature of 25 °C ± 5 °C.
After the water penetration test, no water shall penetrate to the reflecting surface of the retro-reflecting optical unit.
If visual inspection after the water penetration test clearly reveals the presence of water, the retro-reflective device shall not be considered to have passed the test.
The retro-reflector sample device, mounted on a test fixture with initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to the water spray test.
All drain holes and other openings of the retro-reflector device shall remain open during the water spray test.
Drain wicks, when used, shall be tested in the retro-reflector device during the water spray test.

If the retro-reflector is reciprocally incorporated or grouped with signalling or lighting functions, these functions shall be operated during the water spray test at design voltage according to a cycle of 5 min ON (in flashing mode, where appropriate), 55 min OFF.
The water spray test of the retro-reflector device shall last 12 hours (12 cycles of 5/55 min).

After the water spray test and drain period, no standing pool of water shall be formed in the interior of the retro-reflector device, nor shall one be able to be formed by tapping or tilting the device.

After the water spray test and drain period, the RI of the retro-reflector device shall be measured according to the method specified in Part 1 of Annex 4 after drying the exterior of the device with a dry cotton cloth.
The retro-reflector sample device, mounted on a test fixture with its initial RI measured and recorded, shall be subjected to the dust exposure test.

Retro-reflective devices shall be so designed that they retain the prescribed photometric and colorimetric characteristics despite the humidity and corrosive influences to which they are normally exposed, with resistance to corrosion as described in ISO Standard 9227:2017.

The front surface of the retro-reflective device shall resist tarnishing and the protection of the rear face shall resist deterioration, particularly when an essential metal component seems liable to be attacked.

The retro-reflective device, or the lamp if the device is combined with a light, stripped of all removable parts, shall withstand the action of a saline mist for a period of 50 hours, comprising two periods of exposure of 24 hours each, separated by an interval of two hours during which the sample is allowed to dry.

In the case of retro-reflective devices with essential metal components susceptible to corrosion, the device shall withstand a saline mist produced by atomizing, at a temperature of 35 °C ± 2 °C, a saline solution obtained by dissolving 5 parts by weight of sodium chloride in 95 parts of distilled water containing not more than 0.02 per cent of impurities.
Immediately after completion of the corrosion test, the retro-reflective device sample shall not show signs of excessive corrosion liable to impair the efficiency of the device.
Retro-reflective devices shall be subjected to accelerated artificial weathering exposure in accordance with EN ISO 4892-2:2013, using the parameters given in Table A6-1, for a period of 500 hours.
The retro-reflective device shall be subjected to the fuel resistance test using a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol.

Where the fuel resistance test is applied with a test mixture of 70 vol. per cent of n-heptane and 30 vol. per cent of toluol, the outer surface of the retro-reflective device, and in particular of the illuminating surface, lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in the test mixture shall not show any apparent surface changes when inspected visually after about five minutes, except that slight surface cracks will not be objected to.

For moulded plastics reflectors as Classes IA, IB, IIIA, IIIB, IVA and advance warning triangle of type 1, the retro-reflective device shall meet the RI requirements measured according to paragraph 5.1.3.2.2. after its outer surface, and in particular the illuminating surface, has been lightly wiped with a cotton cloth soaked in a detergent lubricating oil and cleaned after about 5 minutes.
The approval number on the retro-reflective device shall be placed close to, but in any position in relation to, the circle surrounding the letter "E".
The digits constituting the approval number on the retro-reflective device shall face the same way as the "E".
The group of symbols indicating the class on the retro-reflective device shall be diametrically opposite the approval number.

Where a device is required to emit "white" light, the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) of the light emitted shall lie inside the chromaticity area defined by the boundaries W12 green boundary y = 0.150 + 0.640 x, W23 yellowish green boundary y = 0.440, W34 yellow boundary x = 0.500, W45 reddish purple boundary y = 0.382, W56 purple boundary y = 0.050 + 0.750 x and W61 blue boundary x = 0.310, with intersection points W1 (0.310, 0.348), W2 (0.453, 0.440), W3 (0.500, 0.440), W4 (0.500, 0.382), W5 (0.443, 0.382) and W6 (0.310, 0.283), according to CIE Publication 15.2, 1986, the CIE 1931 standard colorimetric observer.

Where a device is required to emit "red" light, the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) of the light emitted shall lie inside the chromaticity area defined by the boundaries R12 yellow boundary y = 0.335, R23 the spectral locus, R34 the purple line (its linear extension across the purple range of colours between the red and the blue extremities of the spectral locus) and R41 purple boundary y = 0.980 – x, with intersection points R1 (0.645, 0.335), R2 (0.665, 0.335), R3 (0.735, 0.265) and R4 (0.721, 0.259).

Where a device, excluding retro-reflective tires according to UN Regulation No. 88, is required to retro-reflect "red" light at night-time, the chromaticity coordinates (x,y) of the light reflected shall lie inside the chromaticity area defined by the boundaries R12 yellow boundary y = 0.335, R23 the spectral locus, R34 the purple line and R41 purple boundary y = 0.978 - x, with intersection points R1 (0.643, 0.335), R2 (0.665, 0.335), R3 (0.735, 0.265) and R4 (0.720, 0.258).

The lighting and light-signalling devices shall be so fitted that under normal conditions of use as defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and notwithstanding any vibrations to which they may be subjected, they retain the characteristics prescribed by UN Regulation No. 48 and enable the vehicle to comply with its requirements.
It shall not be possible for the lamps to be inadvertently maladjusted.

For all light-signalling devices, including those mounted on the side panels, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the bearing plane of the vehicle on the road, with a tolerance of ±3°.

For all signalling devices other than side retro-reflectors and side-marker lamps, the reference axis of the lamp when fitted to the vehicle shall be parallel to the median longitudinal plane of the vehicle, with a tolerance of ±3°.
Light-signalling devices shall be fitted in compliance with any specific instructions as regards fitting laid down by the manufacturer.

In the absence of specific instructions, the height and orientation of the lamps shall be verified with the vehicle unladen and placed on a flat, horizontal surface, in the condition defined in paragraphs 2.3.10., 2.3.10.1. and 2.3.10.2. and, in the case where an AFS is installed, with the system in its neutral state.
In the absence of specific instructions, lamps constituting a pair shall have substantially identical photometric characteristics, except for a matched pair of a function and/or an AFS.
On vehicles whose external shape is asymmetrical, the general installation requirements for lamps shall be satisfied so far as is possible.

Lamps grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated with one another shall fulfil all requirements regarding colour, position, orientation, geometric visibility, electrical connections and other requirements, if any.
The photometric and colorimetric requirements of a lamp shall be fulfilled when all other functions with which this lamp is grouped, combined or reciprocally incorporated are switched OFF.

Where a front or rear position lamp is reciprocally incorporated with one or more other function(s) which can be switched ON together with them, the requirements regarding colour of each of these other functions shall be fulfilled when the reciprocally incorporated function(s) and the front or rear position lamps are switched ON.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.14.11.1., subparagraph (a), the apparent surface of which is composed of two or more distinct parts, other than a single retro-reflector, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the total area of the projection of the distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis on a plane tangent to the exterior surface of the outer lens and perpendicular to the reference axis occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projection of the said apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of two adjacent/tangential distinct parts of the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.

Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (b) or (c), composed of two lamps marked "D" or two independent retro reflectors, shall be installed in such a way that either (a) the projection of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of the two lamps or retro reflectors occupies not less than 60 per cent of the smallest quadrilateral circumscribing the projections of the said apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis, or (b) the minimum distance between the facing edges of the apparent surfaces in the direction of the reference axis of two lamps or two independent retro reflectors does not exceed 75 mm when measured perpendicularly to the reference axis.
Single lamps as defined in paragraph 2.4.11.1., subparagraph (d) shall fulfil the requirements of paragraph 5.7.2.1.

Where two or more lamps and/or two or more separate apparent surfaces are included into the same lamp body and/or have a common outer lens, these shall not be considered as an interdependent lamp system, except that a lamp in the shape of a band or strip may be part of an interdependent lamp system.

In the absence of specific instructions, the photometric characteristics (e.g. intensity, colour, apparent surface, etc.) of a lamp shall not be intentionally varied during the period when the lamp is switched ON.

Where the photometric characteristics of a lamp vary in relation to the ambient light, as a consequence of other lamps being switched ON or OFF, or when the lamp is being used to provide another lighting function, any variation in the photometric characteristics shall be in compliance with the technical provisions for the lamp concerned.
Red light emitted by a lamp fitted on the rear of the vehicle (as defined in paragraph 2.1.5.) shall not be visible from the front of the vehicle.

With the exception of a red rearmost side-marker lamp, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a red lamp if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 1 in a transverse plane situated 25 m in front of the vehicle (see Annex 4).

With the exception of reversing lamps and white side conspicuity markings, there shall be no direct visibility of the apparent surface of a white lamp towards the rear of the vehicle if viewed by an observer moving within Zone 2 in a transverse plane situated 25 m behind the vehicle (see Annex 4).

In case of doubt, the requirement on visibility of white light towards the rear shall be deemed fulfilled if the luminous intensity of the white light emitted to the rear, as verified during type approval of the lamps, is not more than 0.25 cd per lamp taking into account the influence of the vehicle body if applicable.

The electrical connections shall be such that the front and rear position lamps, the end-outline marker lamps, if they exist, the side-marker lamps, if they exist, and the rear registration plate lamp can only be switched ON and OFF simultaneously.
The concealment of lamps shall be prohibited, with the exception of the main-beam headlamps, the dipped-beam headlamps and the front fog lamps, which may be concealed when they are not in use.
The colour of the light emitted by the reversing lamp shall be white.
The colour of the light emitted by the stop lamp shall be red.
The colour of the light emitted by the rear position lamp shall be red.
The colour of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be red.
The number of lamps mounted on the vehicle shall be equal to the number indicated in the individual specifications of UN R48.
Any lamp may be installed on movable components only provided that the conditions specified in paragraphs 5.18., 5.19. and 5.20. are fulfilled.

Where rear position lamps, rear direction-indicators or rear retro-reflectors, triangular as well as non-triangular, are installed on movable components and additional lamps for the above functions are fitted and are switched ON when the movable component is in any fixed open position, these additional lamps shall satisfy all the position, geometric visibility and photometric requirements applicable to the lamps installed on the movable component.
When the movable components are in a position other than a "normal position of use", the devices installed on them shall not cause undue discomfort to road users.

When a lamp is installed on a movable component and the movable component is in the "normal position(s) of use", the lamp shall always return to the position(s) specified by the manufacturer in accordance with UN R48.

The apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors shall not be hidden more than 50 per cent by any movable component, with or without a light-signalling device installed on it, in any fixed position (the stable or natural rest position(s) of the movable component specified by the vehicle manufacturer, whether locked or not) different from the "normal position of use", unless this is not practicable and the alternative provisions are met.

Where it is not practicable to keep the apparent surface of front and rear position lamps, front and rear direction-indicator lamps and retro-reflectors hidden by not more than 50 per cent by a movable component, additional lamps satisfying all the position, geometric visibility, colorimetric and photometric requirements for these lamps shall be switched ON when the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis of these lamps is more than 50 per cent hidden by the movable component.

Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is used, the replacement function in case of a failure shall be similar in colour, main intensity and position to the function that has ceased to operate.
Where a temporary fail-safe replacement of the light-signalling function of a rear position lamp is used, the replacement device shall remain operational in its original safety function.

For vehicles of M and N categories, when the electrical system of the vehicle is in a constant voltage operating condition, the voltage supplied at the terminals of devices which, according to their type approval documentation, have been tested by the application of a special power supply/electronic light source control gear, or in a secondary operating mode or at a voltage requested by the applicant, shall not exceed the voltage specified for the relevant devices or functions as they have been approved.

For vehicles of M and N categories with 6 Volt-Systems, in all cases of electric power supply conditions not covered by the special power supply provisions, the voltage at the terminals of the device(s) or function(s) shall not exceed 6.75 V by more than 3 per cent, the means of controlling the maximum voltage being permitted within the body of the device.

There shall be no obstacle on the inside of the angles of geometric visibility to the propagation of light from any part of the apparent surface of the lamp observed from infinity, except for obstacles already presented when the lamp was type-approved.

If, when the lamp is installed, any part of the apparent surface of the lamp is hidden by any further parts of the vehicle, the part of the lamp not hidden by obstacles shall still conform to the photometric values prescribed for the approval of the device.

When the vertical angle of geometric visibility below the horizontal may be reduced to 5° (lamp at less than 750 mm above the ground measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.), the photometric field of measurements of the installed optical unit may be reduced to 5° below the horizontal.

All lamps (devices) shall, where applicable, be type approved according to the corresponding device Regulations as specified in the relevant subparagraphs of paragraph 6 of UN R48 when installed on a vehicle.
The number of reversing lamps on motor vehicles of category M1 and on all other vehicles with a length not exceeding 6,000 mm shall be one device mandatory and a second device optional.
The reversing lamps shall be type-approved according to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 23, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.
The reversing lamp shall be positioned in height not less than 250 mm and not more than 1,200 mm above the ground.

The reversing lamp shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle, except that, if installed, the two optional devices mentioned in paragraph 6.4.2.2. may be fitted on the side of the vehicle provided that the requirements of paragraphs 6.4.5.2. and 6.4.6.2. are fulfilled.

The electrical connections of the reversing lamp shall be such that the lamp can be switched ON only if the reverse gear is engaged and if the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is in such a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.

The reversing lamp shall not switch ON or remain ON if either the reverse gear is not engaged or the device which controls the starting and stopping of the propulsion system is not in a position that operation of the propulsion system is possible.
The number of stop lamps shall be two S1 or S2 category devices and one S3 or S4 category device on all categories of vehicles.
The stop lamp devices shall be type-approved according to the 02 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 7, or to the 00 or subsequent series of amendments to UN Regulation No. 148.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, for S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

For S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the mounting height above the ground shall be not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm, or 2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed.

If the optional stop lamps are installed, they shall be positioned at a height compatible with the requirements of the width and the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.

For S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the horizontal angle of geometric visibility shall be 45° to the left and to the right of the longitudinal axis of the vehicle, except that for stop lamps of categories S1 and S2 mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.
For S1 or S2 category stop lamps, the vertical angle of geometric visibility shall be 15° above and below the horizontal.
Where an S1 or S2 category stop lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to paragraph 5.8.1.), the downward vertical angle of geometric visibility of 15° may be reduced to 5°.
All stop lamps shall be switched ON simultaneously when the braking system provides the relevant signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.

For the rear position lamp, other than the optional rear lamps, the point on the apparent surface in the direction of the reference axis which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

The rear position lamp shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 350 mm nor more than 1,500 mm (2,100 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 1,500 mm and if the optional lamps are not installed).

If the optional rear position lamps are installed, they shall be placed at a height compatible with the applicable width position requirements, the symmetry of the lamps, and at a vertical distance as large as the shape of the bodywork makes it possible, but not less than 600 mm above the mandatory lamps.
The rear position lamp shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.

The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° inwards and 80° outwards, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

The geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°, and where an optional lamp is mounted above 2,100 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the upward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles, as an alternative at the discretion of the manufacturer and only if a rear side-marker lamp is installed on the vehicle, the geometric visibility of the rear position lamp shall have a horizontal angle of 45° outwards to 45° inwards, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the inward angle of 45° may be reduced to 20° under the H plane.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles using this alternative geometric visibility, the rear position lamp shall have a vertical angle of 15° above and below the horizontal, except that where a lamp is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 15° may be reduced to 5°.

For M1 and N1 category vehicles using this alternative geometric visibility, to be considered visible the rear position lamp shall provide an unobstructed view of the apparent surface of at least 12.5 square centimetres, excluding the illuminating surface area of any retro-reflector that does not transmit light.
A closed-circuit tell-tale for the rear position lamps shall be mandatory, except when daytime running lamps are switched ON.
The closed-circuit tell-tale of the rear position lamps shall be combined with that of the front position lamps.
A tell-tale indicating failure of the rear position lamps shall be mandatory if required by the component Regulation.
The non-triangular rear retro-reflector shall be mandatory on motor vehicles.

For the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, the point on the illuminating surface which is farthest from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane shall not be more than 400 mm from the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be positioned in height above the ground not less than 250 mm nor more than 900 mm (not more than 1,200 mm if grouped with any rear lamp(s), 1,500 mm if the shape of the bodywork makes it impossible to keep within 900 mm or 1,200 mm respectively).
The rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be positioned in length at the rear of the vehicle.
The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be a horizontal angle of 30° inwards and outwards.

The geometric visibility of the rear retro-reflector, non-triangular, shall be a vertical angle of 10° above and below horizontal, except that where the retro-reflector is mounted below 750 mm (measured according to the provisions of paragraph 5.8.1.) the downward angle of 10° may be reduced to 5°.
When daytime running lamps are switched ON, the rear position lamps shall be switched ON, and any other lamp(s) mentioned in paragraph 5.11. may also be switched ON.

The rear position lamps and the other lamp(s) mentioned in paragraph 5.11. may be switched OFF when the daytime running lamps are switched ON, and may remain switched OFF only as long as the ambient light conditions outside the vehicle are above 7,000 lux (measured according to the requirements of Annex 13).
The emergency stop signal shall be present on motor vehicles.
The emergency stop signal shall be given by the simultaneous operation of all the stop or direction-indicator lamps fitted as described in paragraph 6.23.7.
All the lamps of the emergency stop signal shall flash in phase at a frequency of 4.0 ± 1.0 Hz.
The emergency stop signal shall operate independently of other lamps.
The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON and OFF automatically.

The emergency stop signal shall be switched ON only when the vehicle speed is above 50 km/h and the braking system is providing the emergency braking logic signal defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the emergency braking logic signal as defined in UN Regulations Nos. 13 and 13-H is no longer provided.
The emergency stop signal shall be automatically switched OFF if the hazard warning signal is activated.

The visibility of a red lamp to the front and of a white lamp to the rear, as referred to in paragraph 5.10.4., shall be assessed within zones 1 and 2 bounded in height by two horizontal planes 1 m and 2.2 m respectively above the ground, and in width by two vertical planes which, forming to the front and to the rear respectively an angle of 15° outwards from the vehicle's median longitudinal plane, pass through the point or points of contact of vertical planes parallel to the vehicle's median longitudinal plane delimiting the vehicle's overall width, the foremost point of contact corresponding to the forward plane and the rearmost to the rearward plane where there are several points of contact.

The position of lamps, as defined in paragraph 2.1.6., in width, in height and in length shall comply with the general requirements set out in paragraphs 2.10.2., 2.10.3., 2.10.4., 2.3.3. and 5.4., such that the measured distances fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The measured angles of geometric visibility of the lamps, checked in accordance with paragraph 2.10.7., shall fulfil the individual specifications applicable to each lamp, except that the limits of the angles may have an allowance corresponding to the ±3° variation permitted in paragraph 5.3. for the mounting of the light-signalling devices.
The visibility of red light towards the front and of white light towards the rear shall comply with paragraph 5.10. of UN R48.

When every lamp supplied by the electrical system of the vehicle is switched on, the lamps and tell-tales shall function in accordance with the provisions set out in paragraphs 5.11. to 5.14. of UN R48 and with the individual specifications applicable to each lamp.

The presence, number, colour, arrangement and, where applicable, the category of lamps, as verified by visual inspection of the lamps and their markings, shall be such that the requirements set out in paragraphs 5.15. and 5.16. of UN R48 and in the individual specifications applicable to each lamp are fulfilled.
